In the battle of Cedar Creek, on the 19th of October, the Eighteenth was
engaged from early dawn until evening, when it participated with the brigade
in a brilliant charge, which closed the struggle and swept from the enemy's
grasp his guns and trains. This single brigade was accredited with the cap-
ture of forty-five pieces. The loss in the engagement was three killed and five
wounded. On the 12th of ]!^ovember the division again met the enemy's cav-
alry near Cedar Creek. The brigade charged and drove him three miles. The
Second Brigade, which charged on a parallel road, was repulsed, and the enemy,
following up, came in upon ihe Eighteenth unawares, capturing Major Phillips,
winter-quarters near Harper's Ferry. It subsequently participated in the de-
scent upon Waynesboro, whereby the remnants of Early's army were captured,
taken, amounting to fifteen hundred, back to Winchester. On the way Gen-
